details: CONFIRMED. The brief asks to check every scenario for the shape "a grader reads the main tree while the change lives on
a task branch". tests-pass is that shape: grade() runs it with cwd=workspace, and bun does not scan .worktrees/, so it
runs the fixture's 4 original tests. The failing bench run shows it: judge-fable add-function run 1 tests-pass passed
with "Ran 4 tests across 1 file" while the passing runs ran 7. Before this change a branch build scored 0.6 on these
three graders whatever its quality; after it, a branch build scores full marks even when its tests fail, so the
correctness half of the scenario no longer measures the branch's code. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: results.json 2026-10-30T02-38-10Z: judge-fable add-function 1 tests-pass True 'Ran 4 tests across 1 file'; active runs 'Ran 7 tests'.
Scratch repro (scaffold, worktree wt/remove-item with a wrong removeItem and a failing test, committed):
tests-pass True exit 0: Ran 4 tests across 1 file. [20.00ms]

pass_cases: 1. removeItem and a failing test only on wt/remove-item, main tree untouched -> tests-pass False.

3. removeItem and passing tests merged into the workspace (main tree) -> tests-pass True (today's passing runs: "Ran 7 tests").

reason: tests/test_bench.py:281 failing branch gives tests-pass False (fails on old toml); 286, 291, 299 cover the other cases and pass.

details: CONFIRMED by reading the command: d=$(mktemp -d) inside the loop, no rm or trap. Harmless today, grows with every bench.
failing_case: small-script run where bin/count is only on a task branch: the loop calls mktemp -d for wt/bench and for wt/<task>
and never removes them; each bench run leaves 1-2 folders behind (TMPDIR already holds 8817 tmp.* folders).
fix_hint: rm -rf "$d" after t "$d" (keep its exit status), or one mktemp -d before the loop with trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT.
pass_cases: 1. bin/count only on wt/count -> script-runs True and no new folder left in TMPDIR.
2. bin/count in the workspace -> script-runs True, no mktemp at all (unchanged).
3. bin/count nowhere -> script-runs False, no folder left.
